Single-cell transcriptomics of embryonic cortex in Gatad2b mutant mice identifies misexpression of Bcl11b, Nfia, H3f3b and Sox5, all regulators of cortical identity and all themselves associated with neurodevelopmental syndromes.
The binding here reads the lesion as loss of repression, since NuRD's role at these promoters is to damp transcription. Misexpression in the source goes in both directions, so that reading is a simplification of what was measured. The cell-type binding is likewise a generalisation: the sequencing was of whole embryonic cortex, which contains progenitors as well as neurons, so "neuron" is the broadest honest label rather than a demonstrated cell of action.

The 50-patient cohort recommends that any child diagnosed with GAND be seen by cardiology, ophthalmology, neurology and developmental specialists, with speech, physical and occupational therapy consultations added. The frequencies in this entry are what make each referral worth making rather than routine: bicuspid aortic valve in 10% with 4% needing cardiac intervention, refractive error and strabismus in the great majority, abnormal brain MRI in 60%, and a wide-based gait in 91% with 61% using orthotics.

evidence.reference_title: GATAD2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (GAND): clinical and molecular insights into a NuRD-related disorder.
evidence.snippet: Seven subjects were identified with missense variants that localized within two conserved region domains (CR1 or CR2) of the GATAD2B protein.

nodes.description: Knockdown restricted to neurons, which is what establishes that the gene is required within neurons rather than in surrounding tissue.
